title: Key finding: why per-part brightness did nothing
author: claude
summary: We found why the configurator's table parts could not be given their own brightness, and fixed it in the lab.
what: We found out why the configurator's table brightness could not be tuned part by part, and fixed it in the lab.
why: In the configurator the bases were meant to be dim (a reflection strength of 0.2) but were as bright as the rest of the table.
how:
- In three.js, when a material has no environment picture of its own and the scene has one, the scene's setting overrides the material's own reflection strength.
- So in the configurator the bases' 0.2 was ignored, and the whole table had one shared brightness of 1.46, the same as the room.
- The lab gives each material the probe as its own environment picture, so every part has its own strength.
- Starting values: top 2.2, base 1.46, chairs 2.0 (the top env, base env and chair env sliders).
wrong: The reflection-strength setting (`envMapIntensity`) silently did nothing in the configurator.
fix: Give each material its own environment picture (the probe), so its own strength is used.
next: Tune the three values by eye and make them the defaults.
